# Deriv-Maestro-Test-Gen 

> Automated workflow for generating Maestro web test cases. All tests go directly in `maestro/` directory with no subfolders. Uses Maestro MCP (Model Context Protocol) for direct device interaction and command reference.

---

## MCP Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `mcp_maestro_cheat_sheet` | Get command syntax and examples |
| `mcp_maestro_run_flow` | Run ad-hoc Maestro commands |
| `mcp_maestro_run_flow_files` | Execute YAML flow files |
| `mcp_maestro_inspect_view_hierarchy` | Get current UI element tree |
| `mcp_maestro_take_screenshot` | Capture device screen |
| `mcp_maestro_tap_on` | Tap UI elements |
| `mcp_maestro_input_text` | Type into focused fields |
| `mcp_maestro_query_docs` | Search Maestro documentation |

### Quick Command Reference

Before writing any Maestro YAML, call the cheat sheet for accurate syntax:

```
mcp_maestro_cheat_sheet()
```

### UI Inspection Before Test Generation

Always inspect the live UI before guessing selectors:

```
mcp_maestro_inspect_view_hierarchy(device_id: "<device_id>")
```

---

## When to Run This Workflow

Trigger test generation when:
- ✅ New UI component added
- ✅ Existing component behavior changed
- ✅ New user flow introduced
- ✅ Button/form/modal added or modified
- ✅ Success/error messages changed

---

## What NOT to Test

**CRITICAL: Only test what was CHANGED, not everything in the file.**

Do NOT create tests for:
- ❌ Existing/unchanged UI elements in a modified file
- ❌ Navigation items that already existed
- ❌ Pre-existing features that weren't modified
- ❌ Boilerplate/wrapper components
- ❌ Elements only tangentially related to the actual change

---

## Workflow Steps

### Step 1: Analyze the Changes

#### 1.1 Detect Modified Files

```bash
# Recent changes (unstaged)
git diff --name-only

# Staged changes
git diff --staged --name-only

# Changes in last commit
git diff HEAD~1 --name-only

# Changes in a feature branch vs main
git diff main...HEAD --name-only
```

#### 1.2 Filter for UI-Related Files

```bash
git diff --name-only | grep -E "\.(tsx|jsx)$"
```

#### 1.3 Identify User-Facing Changes

**⚠️ CRITICAL: Inspect the actual diff, not the entire file!**

```bash
git diff [file]
git diff --staged [file]
```

Search ONLY the changed lines for interactive elements:
- `onClick|onSubmit|onChange|onPress`
- `<Button|<Input|<Form|<Modal`
- `id=`

Search for UI text in changed lines:
- `>\s*[A-Z].*<`
- `label=|placeholder=|title=`
- `toast\(|notify\(|alert\(`

#### 1.4 Verify Change Scope (REQUIRED)

Before proceeding, explicitly list:
1. What was ADDED (new components, new functions, new UI elements)
2. What was MODIFIED (changed behavior, updated text, new props)
3. What was UNCHANGED (existing code that wasn't touched)

> **⛔ STOP: If you cannot clearly identify what was ADDED or MODIFIED, re-read the git diff before proceeding.**

### Step 2: Check Existing Tests

```bash
list_dir: maestro/
grep -l "feature_name" maestro/*.yaml
```

| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| No related test exists | Create new `maestro/[feature]_[action].yaml` |
| Related test exists, new action | Create new file with `runFlow` to existing |
| Related test exists, same action extended | Add steps to existing file |
| Element exists but was NOT changed | ⛔ DO NOT create test |

### Step 3: Inspect the UI

Never guess UI text! Use MCP tools and source code to extract exact strings.

```
mcp_maestro_inspect_view_hierarchy(device_id: "<device_id>")
```

Extract text from:
- Button labels: `<Button>Submit</Button>` → `"Submit"`
- Form labels: `label="Email"` → `"Email"`
- Headings: `<h1>Settings</h1>` → `"Settings"`
- Success/error messages: `toast("Saved!")` → `"Saved!"`

### Step 4: Generate or Extend Test

#### Option A: Create New Test File

```yaml
appId: web
name: "[Feature] - [Action description]"
url: ${BASE_URL}

env:
  BASE_URL: ${MAESTRO_BASE_URL || "https://localhost:8443"}
---
- launchApp
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "[UI element]"
    timeout: 20000
```

#### Option B: Extend Existing Test

```yaml
appId: web
name: "[Feature] - [Extended action]"
url: ${BASE_URL}

env:
  BASE_URL: ${MAESTRO_BASE_URL || "https://localhost:8443"}
---
- runFlow:
    file: [existing_test].yaml
    env:
      BASE_URL: ${BASE_URL}
- tapOn:
    text: "[New UI element]"
```

### Step 5: Write the File

```
write: maestro/[feature]_[action].yaml
```

---

## Command Reference

| Command | Purpose | Example |
|---------|---------|---------|
| `launchApp` | Start browser session | `- launchApp` |
| `tapOn` | Click element | `- tapOn: "Log in"` |
| `inputText` | Type into focused field | `- inputText: "user@email.com"` |
| `extendedWaitUntil` | Wait for element | See below |
| `assertVisible` | Verify element exists | `- assertVisible: "Dashboard"` |
| `assertNotVisible` | Verify element is gone | `- assertNotVisible: "Loading"` |
| `runFlow` | Reuse another flow | `- runFlow: file: other.yaml` |
| `swipe` | Drag/swipe gesture | `- swipe: start: 40%,50% end: 80%,50%` |

---

## Flow Templates

### Auth Flow Template

Use for login, signup, or first app launch:

```yaml
appId: web
name: "Login - Basic authentication"
url: ${BASE_URL}

env:
  BASE_URL: ${MAESTRO_BASE_URL || "https://localhost:8443"}
  USER_EMAIL: ${MAESTRO_USER_EMAIL || "user@example.com"}
  USER_PASSWORD: ${MAESTRO_USER_PASSWORD || "password"}
---
- launchApp
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "Log in"
    timeout: 20000
- tapOn:
    text: "Next"
    repeat: 3
- tapOn:
    text: "Got it"
    repeat: 3
- tapOn:
    text: "Log in"
- tapOn:
    text: "Email"
- inputText: ${USER_EMAIL}
- tapOn:
    text: "Password"
- inputText: ${USER_PASSWORD}
- tapOn:
    text: "Log in"
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "Dashboard"
    timeout: 30000
```

### Sidebar Flow Template

Use for sidebar panel interactions (NO onboarding dismissal needed):

```yaml
appId: web
name: "[Panel name] - Open panel"
url: ${BASE_URL}

env:
  BASE_URL: ${MAESTRO_BASE_URL || "https://localhost:8443"}
---
- launchApp
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "[Sidebar item text]"
    timeout: 20000
- tapOn:
    id: "[sidebar_item_id]"
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "[Panel header text]"
    timeout: 10000
- assertVisible: "[Expected content]"
```

### Extended Flow Template

Use when building on an existing flow:

```yaml
appId: web
name: "[Feature] - [Extended action]"
url: ${BASE_URL}

env:
  BASE_URL: ${MAESTRO_BASE_URL || "https://localhost:8443"}
---
- runFlow:
    file: [base_flow].yaml
    env:
      BASE_URL: ${BASE_URL}
- tapOn:
    text: "[New action]"
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "[Expected result]"
    timeout: 10000
```

---

## Selector Strategy

### Default: Use `text`
```yaml
- tapOn:
    text: "Submit"
```

### Fallback 1: Use `id` (proper HTML id attribute only)
```yaml
- tapOn:
    id: "submit-button"
```

> **⚠️ Use proper `id` attributes only!**
> - ✅ Use actual HTML `id` attribute (e.g., `id="form-firstname"`)
> - ❌ Do NOT use `data-testid` values as `id`

### Fallback 2: Use `index` (multiple matching elements)
```yaml
- tapOn:
    text: "Next"
    index: 0
```

### Fallback 3: Use `repeat` (for onboarding/dialogs)
```yaml
- tapOn:
    text: "Got it"
    repeat: 3
```

---

## Waiting Strategy

**Always use `extendedWaitUntil`** — never fixed timeouts.

### Wait for element to appear
```yaml
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "Submit Button"
    timeout: 15000
```

### Wait for element to disappear
```yaml
- extendedWaitUntil:
    notVisible: "Loading..."
    timeout: 10000
```

### Bad vs Good
```yaml
# ❌ BAD - Fixed timeout, unreliable
- tapOn: "Load"
- waitForAnimationToEnd:
    timeout: 5000

# ✅ GOOD - Waits for actual content
- tapOn: "Load"
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "Data"
    timeout: 15000
```

---

## Flow Composition

Reuse flows with `runFlow`:

```yaml
appId: web
name: "Save user settings"
url: ${BASE_URL}

env:
  BASE_URL: ${MAESTRO_BASE_URL || "https://localhost:8443"}
---
- runFlow:
    file: settings_open.yaml
    env:
      BASE_URL: ${BASE_URL}
- tapOn:
    text: "First Name"
- inputText: "TestUser"
- tapOn:
    text: "Save"
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "Settings saved"
    timeout: 10000
```

---

## File Naming

| Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|
| `feature_action.yaml` | `settings_open.yaml` |
| `flow_subflow.yaml` | `login_oauth.yaml` |
| `component_test.yaml` | `chart_zoom.yaml` |

---

## Environment Variables

Default `BASE_URL` is `https://localhost:8443`.

```yaml
env:
  BASE_URL: ${MAESTRO_BASE_URL || "https://localhost:8443"}
  USER_EMAIL: ${MAESTRO_USER_EMAIL || "default@example.com"}
```

Override for different environments:

```bash
# Local development (default)
maestro test maestro/login.yaml

# Staging
MAESTRO_BASE_URL="https://staging.example.com" maestro test maestro/login.yaml

# Production
MAESTRO_BASE_URL="https://app.example.com" maestro test maestro/login.yaml
```

---

## Flow Types

| Flow Type | Description | Requires Onboarding Dismissal? |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------------------|
| `auth` | Login, signup, password reset | Yes |
| `sidebar` | Sidebar panel interactions | No |
| `navigation` | Page-to-page navigation | No |
| `form` | Form fill and submit | No |
| `modal` | Modal/dialog interactions | No |

---

## Common Patterns

### Login Flow
```yaml
- launchApp
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "Log in"
    timeout: 20000
- tapOn: "Log in"
- tapOn:
    id: "EmailInput"
- inputText: ${USER_EMAIL}
- tapOn:
    id: "PasswordInput"
- inputText: ${USER_PASSWORD}
- tapOn:
    text: "Log in"
- extendedWaitUntil:
    visible: "Dashboard"
    timeout: 30000
```

### Form Fill
```yaml
- tapOn:
    text: "First Name"
- inputText: "John"
- tapOn:
    text: "Last Name"  
- inputText: "Doe"
- tapOn:
    text: "Save"
```

### Dismiss Onboarding Dialogs
**Only for auth flows or first-time app launch:**
```yaml
- tapOn:
    text: "Next"
    repeat: 3
- tapOn:
    text: "Got it"
    repeat: 2
```

### Slider Interaction
```yaml
- tapOn:
    id: "volume_slider"
- swipe:
    start: 40%,50%
    end: 80%,50%
    duration: 800
```

---

## Guardrails Checklist

### Change Verification (REQUIRED)
- [ ] Reviewed git diff to identify ONLY changed code
- [ ] Listed what was ADDED vs MODIFIED vs UNCHANGED
- [ ] Confirmed this test is for CHANGED functionality, not existing
- [ ] Did NOT create tests for navigation/boilerplate that wasn't changed

### Test Quality
- [ ] Checked `maestro/` for existing related tests
- [ ] Identified flow type (auth/sidebar/navigation/form/modal)
- [ ] All `tapOn` use `text:` first (fallback to `id:` if needed)
- [ ] Using `extendedWaitUntil` for waits (not fixed timeouts)
- [ ] Timeout values are reasonable (15-30s for page loads)
- [ ] Flows are atomic (one purpose per file)
- [ ] Reusing existing flows via `runFlow` (no duplication)
- [ ] Text strings match the actual UI (no guessing)
- [ ] No unnecessary onboarding dismissal

> **⛔ STOP: If any "Change Verification" checkbox fails, do NOT create the test.**

---

## Running Tests

### Validate Syntax First
```
mcp_maestro_check_flow_syntax(flow_yaml: "<your_yaml_content>")
```

### Run via MCP
```
mcp_maestro_run_flow_files(device_id: "<device_id>", flow_files: "maestro/login.yaml")
mcp_maestro_run_flow(device_id: "<device_id>", flow_yaml: "- tapOn: 'Submit'")
```

### Run via CLI
```bash
maestro test maestro/login.yaml
maestro test maestro/
MAESTRO_BASE_URL="https://localhost:8443" maestro test maestro/login.yaml
```

---

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Element not found by text | Use `mcp_maestro_inspect_view_hierarchy()` or use `id:` selector |
| Multiple elements match | Add `index: 0` (or 1, 2...) |
| Timeout waiting for element | Increase `timeout` or check element text |
| Flow fails silently | Add `assertVisible` after critical steps |
| Need to dismiss multiple dialogs | Use `repeat: N` on `tapOn` |
| Unsure of command syntax | Call `mcp_maestro_cheat_sheet()` |
| YAML syntax errors | Validate with `mcp_maestro_check_flow_syntax()` |

---

## MCP Quick Reference

### Get Full Command Syntax
```
mcp_maestro_cheat_sheet()
```

### Query Specific Documentation
```
mcp_maestro_query_docs(question: "How do I wait for an element?")
mcp_maestro_query_docs(question: "What selectors are available?")
```

### Inspect Live UI
```
mcp_maestro_inspect_view_hierarchy(device_id: "<device_id>")
```

### Run Ad-hoc Commands
```
mcp_maestro_run_flow(device_id: "<device_id>", flow_yaml: "- tapOn: 'Submit'")
```

### Execute Flow Files
```
mcp_maestro_run_flow_files(device_id: "<device_id>", flow_files: "maestro/settings_open.yaml")
```
